title: "Files Panel"
subtitle: "⌘⇧F: the project's folder as a tree, a pane for any file, and git on top of it."

{{< include _sk/files.html >}}

## The tree {.i-tree-view}

The project's folder, with git's marks on it: a letter on a changed file,
a dot on a folder with changes under it, ignored files dimmed. It works
like a file manager: drag in from Finder, drag rows to move them, cut,
copy, duplicate, remove ([⌘⌫]{.kbd}, to the Trash) and undo
([⌘Z]{.kbd}). New File and New Folder are at the head, and a file the
agent writes appears as it lands.

## Open and edit {.i-file-text}

Click a file and it opens in a pane between the tree and the
chat; click it again to put it away. The enlarge button gives the
pane the chat's room. [⌘S]{.kbd} saves, [⌘W]{.kbd} closes, and
nothing unsaved is lost without asking. Format on save covers ten
languages and is off until you turn it on.

Code comes with line numbers, colors and a gutter mark per git change,
with a card to see or revert it. Every kind of file is drawn for what it
is:

::: {.types}
- [Code]{.i-file-code} every language, colored
- [Markdown]{.i-file-text} as it reads, or as written
- [CSV and TSV]{.i-file-table} a grid you can edit in place
- [Parquet]{.i-file-table} a table with each column's type
- [Word]{.i-file-text} pages you can type in and format
- [Excel]{.i-file-table} cells with their number formats
- [PowerPoint]{.i-file} slides as they look
- [PDF]{.i-file} sharp at any width, with search and page previews
- [HTML]{.i-file-code} in the system's web view
- [Pictures]{.i-image} at their own size
:::

## Git {.i-git-branch}

In a repository the branch is named at the tree's head. Click it to
switch, make a branch ([⌘⇧N]{.kbd}) or publish one; Fetch and Pull sit
at the list's foot. A switch with uncommitted changes asks whether to
leave them or bring them along, and goes through only when every change
lands where you asked.

The **Changes** pill ([⌘⇧G]{.kbd}) opens the sheet: tick the files, write
the message, commit ([⌘↩]{.kbd}), push ([⌘P]{.kbd}). **History** browses
the commits: Undo takes back the newest while the remote does not have
it, Revert takes back any one as a new commit. Nothing is committed,
pushed or pulled without a click that says so.
